facts.text: MECA Wet Chemistry Cell & AFM was deployed at Vastitas Borealis during Phoenix in 2008.

The Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer included four single-use wet-chemistry beakers filled with Earth water and reagents, optical and atomic force microscopes, and ion-selective electrodes.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Discovered perchlorates (ClO4-) at 0.5% concentration in the soil and measured a mildly alkaline pH of 7.7, comparable to terrestrial asparagus-friendly soil.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Vastitas Borealis.
The discovery of perchlorates explained the puzzling 1976 Viking GCMS results and fundamentally altered understanding of Mars organic chemistry and habitability.
